2026-09-04T03:25:10.4403449Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4404124Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4404696Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4405575Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4406763Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4407863Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4410669Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4414391Z >
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4419311Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4424406Z >
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4425838Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4427902Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4428233Z ### How to Use
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4428661Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4429820Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4431092Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4431912Z ```bash
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4433018Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4434301Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4435917Z ```
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4436321Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4436774Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4438101Z ```bash
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4439051Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4441048Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4442619Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4443981Z ```
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4444344Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4445936Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4447806Z ```bash
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4448795Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4450012Z ```
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4450888Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4451715Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4452781Z ```bash
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4453727Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4455270Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4457300Z ```
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4457694Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4458163Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4458903Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4461461Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4464365Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4464683Z ```bash
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4466069Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4467797Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4469290Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4469847Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4470720Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4472503Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4475424Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4476670Z ```
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4477238Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4478605Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4480854Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4481177Z ```bash
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4482409Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4484489Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4485813Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4486617Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4487535Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4489609Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4490596Z ```
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4490955Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4491345Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4492764Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4494496Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4496768Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4498784Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4501259Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4502228Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4502540Z ### Notes
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4502918Z 
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4504551Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4507322Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4510091Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4512343Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4514477Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4517096Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4518854Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4520610Z </mcp-clis>
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4521317Z <github-context>
2026-09-04T03:25:10.4522382Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:
